decisions.quote:
In 2012, our research team initiated an effort to replicate Tschudin’s follow-up experiments. The goal
was to replicate as much of Tschudin’s methodology as could be determined from the summary in his 2006
paper given that the training protocol used to teach the dolphins, the various aspects of the task, and the timeline
it took to prepare the dolphins for the task, were not provided (Table 3). To fill any gaps in Tschudin’s
methodology, we followed the descriptions for the standardized testing procedure presented in Call and
Tomasello (1999), including limiting the number of FBTs presented so as to control for the effect of experience.
decisions.location: A Case Study - Attempted Replication, p. 10, lines 558-563 (see also Discussion, p. 13, line 654; References, p. 22, lines 1043-1044)
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files (adjudications/12db194db4781556.json, argon/12db194db4781556.state.json) were checked and do not exist; prior expert result (fields_12db194db4781556_000.result.json), independent validation (source_validation_0003.result.json), Crossref metadata (10.1017/s0962728600023563), blind coding, and full primary text were reviewed. Answering the scope objection: Hill et al. (2018) conducted a single 2012 case study and did not independently re-test two separate target papers. Under the codebook replication-chain rule, the target is the closest study actually re-tested: Tschudin (2006), which re-tested the same four dolphins from Tschudin (2001) (plus a fifth naive dolphin) with added controls. The Case Study section explicitly states that the 2012 effort was initiated to replicate Tschudin's follow-up experiments from his 2006 summary, the Discussion explicitly calls the experiment an attempted replication of Tschudin's study (2006), and the protocol implements the 2006 controls (visible displacement trials and modified 'dud' true belief trials, neither of which was conducted in the 2001 pilot, Table 3) plus target-pole tapping. References to Call and Tomasello (1999) and Tschudin (2001) (e.g., planning 12 displacement and 4 FBT trials) supply unstated procedural details to fill gaps in the 2006 report rather than establishing a separate empirical re-test of 2001. Replacing the shipped 2001 entry with Tschudin (2006) and attaching target_index 1 reconciles row 349 with blind target 1 without creating a false missing pair.

decisions.quote:
Tschudin
(2001) reported near perfect performance by four bottlenose dolphins, but upon retesting with additional
controls, the same four dolphins did not perform at levels significantly above chance when their data were
pooled or tested individually (Tschudin, 2006).
In our attempted replication of Tschudin’s study (2006), the bottlenose dolphin tested was unable to
pass the invisible displacement trials, even after experience with visible displacement and what seemed an
extensive training history. Despite sophisticated social structures and naturalistic displays suggesting advanced
social cognition, attempts to capture ToM abilities of primates and dolphins using the original version of the
nonverbal FBT (Call & Tomasello, 1999) have failed continuously.
decisions.location: Discussion, p. 13, lines 650-658 (see also A Case Study - Attempted Replication, p. 13, lines 628-637; Table 3, pp. 6-8)
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files (adjudications/12db194db4781556.json, argon/12db194db4781556.state.json) were checked and do not exist. Evaluating the outcome specifically against the resolved target Tschudin (2006) rather than borrowing the contrast with the positive 2001 pilot: in Tschudin (2006), although the four re-tested dolphins failed to reach statistical significance on FBT trials (9/12, 75%) and a fifth naive dolphin had testing terminated after 166 training trials, the four dolphins passed task training (3/4, Table 3), achieved satisfactory performance in locating the invisibly displaced reward on control trials without an assistive marker (p. 9, Table 3), and succeeded significantly above chance when pooled on True Belief Task (TBT) control trials (10/13, 77%, p. 10, Table 3). In Hill et al.'s (2018) attempted replication of Tschudin (2006), by contrast, training of the second dolphin was halted early and the tested concept-naive dolphin never achieved the prerequisite 80-85% training criterion across 9 months and over 1,000 trials (115/183, 63%), failed the invisible displacement controls (3/7, 43% without communicator; 1/3, 33% with communicator, explicitly contrasted with Tschudin 2006 in the Discussion), failed the ignore-communicator control (1/3, 33%), reached only 12/19 (63%) on modified dud TBT trials, and scored 0/2 (0%) on the two administered FBT trials before the remaining two planned FBT trials were aborted. Both under codebook Rule 1 (the authors' explicit overall verdict characterizing the study in the title, p. 13, and p. 17 as a failure to replicate that failed during training of the prerequisite skills and invisible displacement) and under the codebook rule that failed preliminary/control tests preventing a full test of the focal hypothesis are coded as failed (not uninformative or successful), the outcome for Tschudin (2006) is failed.
